findings.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb:145-151 — `self.downsize` is defined twice; the second 4-arg definition (`from, to, dimensions, opts`) silently replaces the 5-arg one (`from, to, max_width, max_height, opts`), so existing callers passing width and height separately (e.g. `OptimizedImage.create_for` thumbnail generation) send the integer height as `opts`, and `opts[:allow_animation]` raises `TypeError` on an Integer

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client-side size check no longer consults `max_<type>_size_kb`, allowing non-image attachments up to 10MB even when `max_attachment_size_kb` is smaller; the server still enforces the limit, so users get a late, less specific failure after a full upload instead of the immediate pre-upload alert

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64-69 — Up to five synchronous ImageMagick `convert` invocations on a file of up to 10MB run inside the request thread with no timeout or resource limit around `convert_with`, letting users uploading large or pathological images tie up Unicorn workers

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — The 413 handler reports a hardcoded 10MB limit, but 413 comes from the web server whose `client_max_body_size` is configured independently, so the message states a wrong number on any deployment where nginx's limit differs from 10MB

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66-67 — Return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is ignored; if `convert` fails (returns false) the loop retries the same failing command up to five times and then proceeds to `Upload.create_for` with whatever is on disk, possibly a partially written file

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63 — `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` only checks the extension, so a non-image renamed to `.png` is handed to ImageMagick via `convert_with` shell command five times before normal validation runs, providing a cheap way to burn server CPU

app/models/optimized_image.rb, app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb — No specs cover the new auto-downsize loop (file over the limit is reduced, file under the limit is untouched, non-image files skipped) or the changed `optimize`/`downsize`/`resize` signatures; the duplicate-method regression would have been caught by the existing `OptimizedImage.create_for` spec if run against this change

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64-69 — Up to five synchronous ImageMagick `convert` invocations on a file of up to 10MB run inside the request thread with no timeout or resource limit around `convert_with`, letting users uploading large or pathological images tie up Unicorn workers

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new synchronous loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` that can call `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` up to 5 times in the request path (lines ~64-69). `OptimizedImage.downsize` ultimately runs ImageMagick via `convert_with` using a backtick shell call with no timeout or resource limits (shown in `optimized_image.rb`), so an upload of a large/pathological image could repeatedly invoke `convert` and tie up a web worker. This availability/DoS risk is directly introduced/exacerbated by the new loop.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — The 413 handler reports a hardcoded 10MB limit, but 413 comes from the web server whose `client_max_body_size` is configured independently, so the message states a wrong number on any deployment where nginx's limit differs from 10MB

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the 413 handler in `utilities.js` from `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB). A 413 response reflects the server/request-size limit (e.g., nginx), which is not shown as being fixed at 10MB in this diff, so the UI can now report an incorrect max size on deployments where the server limit differs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66-67 — Return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is ignored; if `convert` fails (returns false) the loop retries the same failing command up to five times and then proceeds to `Upload.create_for` with whatever is on disk, possibly a partially written file

adjudication.rationale: The new downsizing loop in `uploads_controller.rb` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` but does not check whether the conversion succeeded. `OptimizedImage.downsize` ultimately calls `convert_with`, which returns `false` on non-zero exit status; on failure the tempfile size may remain unchanged, so the `while ... tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` condition stays true and the loop will retry up to 5 times and then proceed to `Upload.create_for` without guaranteeing a valid/downsized image was produced. Because it overwrites the same path (`from` == `to`), a failure could also leave a corrupted on-disk file that still gets uploaded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63 — `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` only checks the extension, so a non-image renamed to `.png` is handed to ImageMagick via `convert_with` shell command five times before normal validation runs, providing a cheap way to burn server CPU

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a pre-validation downsizing loop gated by `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` and can call `OptimizedImage.downsize` up to 5 times if the file remains oversized. However, the finding’s core assertion—“`FileHelper.is_image?` only checks the extension, so a non-image renamed to .png will be processed”—cannot be verified from this diff because `FileHelper.is_image?`’s implementation is not shown. Therefore the claimed exploitability rests on behavior not present/confirmable in the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb, app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb — No specs cover the new auto-downsize loop (file over the limit is reduced, file under the limit is untouched, non-image files skipped) or the changed `optimize`/`downsize`/`resize` signatures; the duplicate-method regression would have been caught by the existing `OptimizedImage.create_for` spec if run against this change

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial new behavior in `UploadsController#create_upload` (a retry loop that conditionally downsizes images until they fall under `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`) and refactors `OptimizedImage` APIs (`resize`/`downsize` now pass a single dimension string; `optimize` now accepts `dimensions`; plus a new overload-style `downsize(from,to,dimensions,opts)` is introduced). The PR diff contains no corresponding spec changes, so it’s a concrete, diff-grounded testing gap for new logic and a signature refactor that could regress callers. The statement about an existing `OptimizedImage.create_for` spec catching a duplicate-method regression is not verifiable from the diff, but the core “missing coverage for new loop and signature changes” concern is.
